blocks.content: You have shapes on screen. Now it is time to make them move.

The browser gives you a built in function called requestAnimationFrame. It tells the browser to call your drawing function right before it paints the next frame on screen. Most displays refresh 60 times per second, so your function gets called roughly every 16 milliseconds.

14</html>
Click Run Code and you will see a square painting across the canvas. But notice something. It leaves a trail behind it.
That trail is intentional. It is exactly what the next page fixes.

The loop structure is always the same: define a function, call requestAnimationFrame inside it pointing back at itself, then call the function once to start the chain. That single animate() call at the bottom kicks off the whole loop.

blocks.content: Next, you will fix that trail and learn the one line that every animation loop needs.
